ety.text: From за- (za-, “over, covering”) + пон (pon, “stretched cloth, panel of fabric”), thus literally “a cloth placed over (something)." According to Pokorny, the latter is ultimately Proto-Indo-European *(s)penh₁- (“to weave”); see Proto-Slavic *pęti (“to stretch, tile”). Related to Bulgarian по́нява (pónjava), Serbo-Croatian поњава (“bedsheet”).

ety.text: From Old East Slavic парусъ (parusŭ), of uncertain origin. Inherited from Old East Slavic порочныи (poročnyi), from порокъ (porokŭ) + -ныи (-nyi). By surface analysis, поро́к (porók) + -ный (-nyj).
